clue.text: Fixed price: English prescription

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of rigged or doctored, so the letters of price are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopper notes a set price for something English, or a doctor writes a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixed price' reads as a shop term, but 'Fixed' tells you to rearrange PRICE into RECIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A formula telling how to make something is a prescription, especially in older usage for medicines.

clue.text: Tick off salesman over fish

indicators.note: over places the salesman above the fish in a down entry

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A salesperson is told off about the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To tick off is to rebuke or scold, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Chance shifting round one part of track, perhaps

indicators.note: round means the reworked letters surround the numeral
shifting means the letters of chance move about

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A racing driver takes a chance on part of the circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' turns CHANCE into CHCANE; 'round' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight S-bend placed on a motor-racing circuit is one example of a section of track.

clue.text: What's prior up to boiling a mixture of things?

indicators.note: boiling means the letters are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A monastic prior is up to something with a bubbling concoction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up to' looks like 'doing', but its letters join PRIOR as anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A medley or miscellany of assorted items, also the dried petals in a bowl.

clue.text: Elbow joint

definitions.meaning: to elbow is to push your way through, the same as to barge with the upper arm
the ball-and-socket joint at the top of the arm

explanation.surface: A pair of anatomical words, elbow and joint.
explanation.definitionFit: To push past people with the arm is to elbow or barge them, and the upper-arm joint names the same word.

clue.text: Much suffering priest accepting new role very quickly

parts.note: hell is much suffering

indicators.note: accepting means the priest's letters take in the reworked ones

parts.note: Father is the title of a priest

indicators.note: new means the letters of role form a fresh order

explanation.surface: A long-suffering priest is rushed into a new role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much suffering' looks like a description of the priest, but it is a separate piece; 'new' rearranges ORLE and 'accepting' sets it into the priest.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at breakneck speed, recklessly fast.

clue.text: Total, say

definitions.meaning: complete or absolute, as in nonsense
to speak or voice a word

explanation.surface: A sum and a speech verb set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means complete, as a verb it means to speak.

clue.text: Fingerprint expert?

parts.note: a dab is slang for a fingerprint, so a skilled person sounds like someone who handles prints

explanation.surface: A forensic specialist who examines prints.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names someone highly skilled; the clue reads dab as police slang for a print.

clue.text: Find it in tracks artist laid down first?

indicators.note: laid down first puts the artist at the top in a down entry

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician

indicators.note: in means the word it goes inside the railway

parts.note: RY is short for railway, tracks

explanation.surface: An artist lays down his find on the railway tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare and valuable discovery is a find.

clue.text: Rule of law I care about, the result of suffering many blows?

definitions.text: the result of suffering many blows

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A boxer cares about the rule of law despite his injuries.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's swollen, deformed ear is caused by repeated punches.

clue.text: Describe round object in war game

parts.note: to paint a picture in words is to describe
a ball is a round object

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to depict a round object in a battle simulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock combat sport in which players fire pellets of dye at each other is a war game.

clue.text: Row round first of buoys in river

indicators.note: round means the row's letters surround the extra letter

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word buoys

explanation.surface: Someone rows around a buoy on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a verb about boating, but it is TIER, a row of seats; 'round' puts B (from 'first of buoys') inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the river that flows through Rome.

clue.text: Enjoying a run of success playing a wheel?

definitions.meaning: literally performing on something that turns, a wheel being a thing that rolls along

explanation.surface: A lucky gambler is winning at the roulette wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a winning streak; the second reading takes it literally as being upon something that turns.

clue.text: Newspaper covering fields of study in distant countries

indicators.note: covering means the newspaper's letters go around the other piece

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times
areas are fields of study, as in subject areas

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports on research subjects in faraway lands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Financial Times is a British daily printed on pink paper, conventionally FT; 'covering' wraps it round the subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: East Asia is the remote region of countries from a European viewpoint.

clue.text: Explicit about Shakespearean hero

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about
King Lear is the title character of a Shakespeare tragedy

explanation.surface: A frank comment on one of Shakespeare's protagonists.
explanation.definitionFit: Something explicit is plain and unambiguous, stated outright.

clue.text: Home team needs passion up front

indicators.note: up front means this piece comes first, ahead of the team

parts.note: fire is passion or ardour
a side is a team

explanation.surface: The home team needs fervour in its forward line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home team' reads as one phrase, but 'Home' is the definition and 'team' is SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The hearth stands for domestic life, so by the fire means at home.

clue.text: Dope may be easy to obtain, ultimately

parts.note: simple means easy

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of obtain

explanation.surface: Drugs may be readily available in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like drugs but means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Chief character in a line

parts.note: a card is a character, an eccentric person

explanation.surface: The main character is in a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal means principal or fundamental, as in cardinal sins.

clue.text: Italian individual backing pub singer

indicators.note: backing means the following pieces come behind the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
IT is short for Italian, as in vermouth (gin and It)
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: An Italian person supports a pub vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A male voice between tenor and bass, so a type of singer.

clue.text: Commander, awfully mad over broken rail

indicators.note: over places the first piece above the second in a down entry
awfully means the letters of mad are jumbled
broken means the letters of rail are scrambled

explanation.surface: An officer is furious about a damaged railing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' gives ADM from MAD; 'broken' gives IRAL from RAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral commands a fleet, a naval rank.

clue.text: Tea after instant coffee

indicators.note: after means tea's letters follow the instant

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
cha (char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Someone drinks tea, then instant coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instant coffee' looks like one item, but 'instant' gives MO and 'coffee' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of fine coffee, originally from the Yemeni port of Mocha.

clue.text: Depressed prisoner with word of warning

parts.note: a con is a convict
cave, Latin for beware, is old schoolboy slang for look out

explanation.surface: A gloomy inmate is given a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depressed' suggests gloom but means curved inward.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface pressed inward, hollowed, is depressed in the physical sense.

clue.text: Cool cats, initially in tartan

indicators.note: in places that letter within the cloth

parts.note: plaid is tartan cloth

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of cats

explanation.surface: Hip cats wearing tartan.
explanation.definitionFit: Being calm and unruffled is being cool-headed.

clue.text: Give a false impression about alcoholic drink and soft drink

indicators.note: about means the lie's letters surround the drink

parts.note: to lie is to give a false impression
mead is an alcoholic drink of fermented honey

explanation.surface: Someone is deceptive about whether a drink is alcoholic or soft.
explanation.definitionFit: A lime-flavoured non-alcoholic drink is a soft drink.

clue.text: Earmark a tax to be raised

indicators.note: raised means turned upward, so in a down entry the tax reads bottom to top

parts.note: a toll is a charge or tax

explanation.surface: A tax is earmarked for raising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be raised' looks like increasing a tax, but reverses TOLL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To set aside or assign for a purpose is to earmark.

clue.text: Able to grab time with single daughter

parts.note: alone means single, by oneself

explanation.surface: A single parent with a daughter manages to snatch some time.
explanation.definitionFit: Having claws, as a bird of prey does, makes a creature able to grab.

clue.text: Constant test for underwater growth

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A marine biologist keeps testing something growing under the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Reef-forming skeletons of tiny marine polyps build up beneath the sea, a growth underwater.

clue.text: Problem caused by damaged retina, certainly inside

indicators.note: inside means the affirmative goes within the reworked letters
damaged means the letters of retina are broken up and reordered

parts.note: yes means certainly

explanation.surface: An optician says a damaged retina certainly causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges the eye part into ETRAIN, and 'inside' sets the affirmative word within it; the definition 'Problem' hides at the very start.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, aching eyes from overuse is a health complaint, a problem.

clue.text: Brought round, a top Conservative is slow to act

indicators.note: brought round means turned about, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: a lid is a top
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A revived senior Conservative is sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought round' looks like reviving someone but reverses A LID into DILA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tending to delay, procrastinating, is being slow to act.

clue.text: Imagined Lauren being cast

indicators.note: cast as in reshaped or thrown, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lauren dreams of being cast in a role.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imagined is fanciful and not real.
